title: Fail-closed cross-repository Collision Assessor
goal: Guarantee that no Perfect Planner-managed worker can receive an edit claim until an independent read-only assessor has proven a complete, fresh, non-overlapping plan and resource snapshot and every approval has produced a durably delivered signal to its registered originating chat, with only ticket-scoped coordination remaining after discovery access is revoked.

meta.focus: one-time read-only global discovery, deterministic file and resource collision analysis, immutable clearance snapshots, transactional approval-to-chat wake-up, visible head-orchestrator and worker messaging, ticket-only walkie-talkie coordination, forced replanning, and fail-closed worker admission

spine.title: Guarantee and trust boundary
spine.summary: Define exactly what is guaranteed, isolate the assessor from orchestrators and workers, and fail closed outside the proven boundary.

spine.title: Global registry and one-time discovery
spine.summary: Build a machine-wide, read-only census with fresh identities, manifests, leases and a single-use capability that is destroyed after assessment.

spine.title: Deterministic collision proof
spine.summary: Normalize logical paths and resources, derive an immutable conflict graph, and issue a tamper-evident verdict only from complete inputs.

spine.title: Ticket coordination and claim enforcement
spine.summary: Turn conflicts into scoped walkie-talkie tickets, make approval wake its registered originating chat, and make every worker claim cryptographically dependent on both live assessor clearance and confirmed approval delivery.

spine.title: Operator visibility
spine.summary: Put a persistent head orchestrator and chat status above P1, keep every worker conversation visible, put the assessor first in the run flow, and make wait, replan, approval-delivery and decision states impossible to miss.

spine.title: Adversarial certification and rollout
spine.summary: Prove races, stale state, crashes, replay, path tricks and 100-planner load before packaging or calling the guarantee active.

vertebrae.title: Read-only census collectors
vertebrae.notes: Replanned after RED review: board HTTP is display-only and is never an assessor authority. The native collector receives no caller-supplied path, root, URL, port or endpoint. Real collection runs once in a fixed internal child mode of the exact current executable, receives a nonce-bound bounded request through an anonymous stdin pipe, writes a bounded metadata-only response to stdout, and is killed then waited on at deadline so no privileged reader survives capability revocation. The helper reads only exact registry-addressed Planner metadata beneath configured roots, projects a strict DTO immediately, and the parent revalidates generation, digest, filesystem identity and observation time before acceptance. Missing, extra, duplicate, stale, aliased, timed-out or inconsistent input is UNKNOWN.

vertebrae.title: Deterministic collision graph
vertebrae.notes: The analyzer is a pure deterministic function over the B19 canonical claim snapshot. It never reads the filesystem, trusts caller paths or invents a disposition. Exact-file, directory-prefix and canonical resource collisions are evaluated from opaque typed keys. Glob claims are a hard UNKNOWN in v1. WAIT, REPLAN and USER_DECISION are emitted only when the frozen trusted disposition contract explicitly authorizes that result; missing or contradictory policy is UNKNOWN. Reviewer-triggered hardening expands this node to registry.rs solely to seal the COMPLETE registry value behind the native registry validator: production callers can neither fabricate nor mutate a validated complete document before analysis. api.rs is included only for its existing native test to borrow the now-sealed read result without taking ownership; no command or renderer surface changes.

vertebrae.title: Actionable ORCH problem guidance
vertebrae.notes: A red or amber ORCH statement is not actionable unless the operator can identify the exact affected scope and the safest next step. Every ORCH bubble therefore uses an explicit Problem / Where / Remedy contract. Location must name the narrowest truthful repository, plan, branch, node and worker data available. Remedy must preserve fail-closed behavior and must not imply an action was executed merely because it was recommended. The lifecycle-boundary regression case is: start and Perfect Planner execution are usable, but the combined lifecycle remains unsafe until the Planner invokes finish as the authoritative release gate and cleanup remains explicit and last.

vertebrae.title: Single-use native metadata census API

vertebrae.title: Canonical claim snapshot and disposition contract
vertebrae.notes: Corrective prerequisite created after B06 RED review. Native census code derives repository equality from the real linked-worktree .git metadata and a share-restricted handle to the resolved Git common directory; caller repository IDs and paths are never equality authority. It freezes opaque typed ExactFile, DirectoryTree and Resource claims plus machine-issued proposal/active lease, fence, dependency and per-claim disposition evidence before discovery is revoked. The native head orchestrator signs exact-scope authority receipts with an Ed25519 signing key that is never exposed to the census helper; the helper and restart path receive verification-only public authority plus an issuer epoch. Until the later trusted scheduler issuer is integrated, production issuance remains unreachable and therefore UNKNOWN. Tauri startup performs a bounded locked v1-to-v2 verifier-only migration that preserves roots and registrations, increments generation, clears legacy census/authorities and leaves malformed legacy state untouched; later issuer rotation invalidates old receipts without bricking registry recovery. Directory claims use logical segment-prefix ownership and include future children. Planned work remains visible; terminal completed/released work releases ownership claims but remains as a path-free signed dependency tombstone. Cross-plan dependency identities remain globally scoped for B06 to resolve over the full census. Globs are deliberately unsupported in v1 and force UNKNOWN rather than a guessed expansion. Every typed claim, source manifest digest, physical alias edge, aggregate authority-set scope and disposition is bound into the census/input digest.

vertebrae.title: Exclusive scheduler authority issuer
vertebrae.notes: Corrective production bridge required by the B19 adversarial review. B19 deliberately provides verification-only fail-closed plumbing and cannot mint production authority. B20 gives exactly one native scheduler-owned process the signing secret and makes machine authority a projection of the scheduler's locked pre-claim reservation, clearance and delivered approval facts. The scheduler must reserve without granting write authority, publish the complete signed authority set, obtain a fresh census and CLEAR result, then atomically consume the clearance into the worker claim. Renderer, model and worker inputs are never issuer authority. Lock loss, process restart, generation drift, stale fence, partial set, replay, rollback or publication failure remains UNKNOWN and grants no worker. B09 and B12 are hard-dependent on this node.

checklist.text: Persist a non-writing pre-claim reservation containing exact run, node, worker, lease generation, fence, manifest, policy and delivered-approval digests under an operating-system lock plus generation-and-digest CAS

Give exactly one native issuer owner the in-memory Ed25519 signing key and expose only verification authority; restart or owner loss rotates the epoch and leaves admission UNKNOWN until a complete republish

Project the scheduler reservation, immutable clearance and durable approval receipt into one exact complete signed authority set for every registered Planner with no renderer, model or worker issuance path
Enforce reserve then publish then census then CLEAR then atomic clearance-consumption then worker-claim ordering; every failure or crash grants zero write authority and recovers as UNKNOWN
Sign heartbeat, transition and terminal updates without permitting run, worker, fence, manifest, policy, assumption, dependency or disposition drift outside the scheduler's authorized transition

Prove cross-process claim races, lock loss, restart, stale-fence replay, partial publication, rollback and one-hundred-worker mixed conflicting and non-conflicting stress without duplicate ownership or lost authority events

Own snapshot storage through a held physically verified native directory handle with relative no-follow opens, same-handle temp-to-final identity, alias checks and directory fsync; reject ancestor junction, symlink, hardlink and swap attacks

Anchor journal epoch and head outside the journal, retain one exclusive native writer with authenticated checkpoints, and prove sustained one-hundred-agent append latency and memory remain bounded without trusting file length or caller caches
Construct snapshot store, journal anchor, issuer epoch and secret factories atomically in the native owner and zeroize every temporary token or key on all fallible paths
Replace the broker enabled boolean with a non-cloneable process-epoch TicketBrokerAuthority owned only by the native scheduler and bind every route, transition and acknowledgement to that authority
Close crate-internal ticket bypasses by exposing only owner-filtered reads and sealed native-authority append operations before registering any production command

vertebrae.title: Resource-aware PowerShell hazard sentinel
vertebrae.notes: Pre-certification sentinel for completed collision-assessor foundations only. It runs exact allowlisted Rust hazard tests sequentially from PowerShell, validates every test name before execution, gates on host memory and CPU pressure, enforces per-test deadlines, captures durable logs and a JSON report, and never activates production authority. B12 consumes this harness later and remains responsible for B09/B10/B15/B20 end-to-end hazards once those paths exist.
